newsitem.title: USA: US gives antitrust okay to oil firms' R&D venture.
newsitem.headline: US gives antitrust okay to oil firms' R&D venture.

text.p: The U.S. Justice Department said Wednesday it approved a proposal by six major oil firms and a Texas university to set up a research and development joint venture relating to oil exploration and production.
The department's Antitrust Division said the venture, the Petroleum E&P Cooperative, did not appear to be designed to restrict price, output or research competition among members.

"To the extent that the cooperative in fact engages in research efforts that would not be undertaken by individual firms, the joint venture may have the procompetitive effect of promoting innovation," said Joel Klein, acting assistant attorney general in charge of the Antitrust Division.
Initial members of the cooperative are Mobil Corp. Atlantic Richfield Co., Amoco Corp., Texaco Inc., Exxon Corp., the Shell Oil Co. subsidiary of Royal Dutch/Shell Group and Texas A&M University.

The cooperative, which will start with a modest $5 million annual budget, will accept any other oil exploration and production company and does not restrict members from engaging in independent research, the department said. Individual firms will take part in specific joint research projects and Texas A&M will administer and coordinate the effort, it said.
